_comment: The Helm chart delivery option every new version of the AWS Marketplace container product gets (Catalog API, AddDeliveryOptions; automation/aws_catalog.py). The chart runs OneUptime as serviceAccount.name, and reports usage with that service account's IAM role. AWS's launch page leaves ${AWSMP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT} for the buyer to fill in, and its eksctl command attaches a role the buyer already has, naming no policy: the usage instructions give the command that creates the oneuptime service account with a role that may call MeterUsage (AWSMarketplaceMeteringFullAccess). Usage instructions: at most 4,000 characters.
title: Helm chart for Amazon EKS
description: OneUptime Enterprise on Amazon EKS, installed with Helm: uptime monitoring, status pages, on-call, incidents, logs, traces and metrics in one platform, with its own PostgreSQL, ClickHouse and Valkey in the cluster. Guide: https://oneuptime.com/docs/en/installation/cloud-marketplaces
usageInstructions:
Before you install:
1. An Amazon EKS cluster with at least 3 nodes of 4 vCPUs and 16 GiB of memory, the Amazon EBS CSI driver with a default StorageClass, and an IAM OIDC provider:
   eksctl utils associate-iam-oidc-provider --cluster <cluster> --approve
2. The oneuptime service account, with an IAM role that has the AWSMarketplaceMeteringFullAccess policy. Create both with this command, in place of the eksctl command in step 1 of the General launch instructions on this page (that one attaches a role you would have to create first):
   eksctl create iamserviceaccount --name oneuptime --namespace oneuptime --cluster <cluster> --attach-policy-arn arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AWSMarketplaceMeteringFullAccess --approve --override-existing-serviceaccounts
   OneUptime reports its users to AWS Marketplace every hour with this role; without it, the Enterprise features stay off.

Install with the commands in step 2 of the General launch instructions. In the helm install command, set these values:
   serviceAccount.name=oneuptime (the service account above)
   host=<your domain name>, for example oneuptime.example.com
   httpProtocol=https if a certificate is in front of OneUptime, otherwise http

Then point the domain name at the load balancer (the EXTERNAL-IP of the service ending in -nginx: kubectl get service --namespace oneuptime) and open it to create the first account. The first start migrates the database and takes a few minutes. Within the hour, the dashboard's edition label shows the Enterprise Edition, licensed through AWS Marketplace.

To upgrade, run helm upgrade with a newer version of this chart and the same values.

Guide: https://oneuptime.com/docs/en/installation/cloud-marketplaces
Support: https://oneuptime.com/support
